drawDetail.narrative: Kaleiçi's Ottoman lanes drop to the old harbour, Konyaaltı's pebble beach runs for kilometres under the Taurus Mountains, and Perge, Aspendos and the Lycian Way are day trips. Winters are mild and cheap and draw a settled foreign retiree community; July and August are hot (34 °C average highs) and packed with package tourists.

items.label: Rent
items.note: Furnished 1+1 in Konyaaltı or Lara (Güzeloba/Şirinyalı). Live emlakjet asking rents of 28,000–45,000 TL, median about 35,000 TL (about $712 at 49.13 TRY/USD), plus a small premium for 1–3 month terms. Several winter lets end on 1 June.

items.label: Utilities
items.note: Electric, water and home internet. Wise gives £67 utilities plus £10 internet for an 85 m² flat (about $102 at 0.756 GBP/USD), scaled down for a 55–65 m² 1+1. Summer air-con pushes bills up.

items.label: Groceries
items.note: Home cooking. Wise gives £160/month per person (about $212); Migros/BİM plus weekly pazars.

items.label: Eating out
items.note: Derived: about 14 meals out at about $9 (Wise: inexpensive meal £6) plus about 15 café coffees at about $3.50.

items.label: Local transport
items.note: Official full fare is 42 TL per boarding with Antalyakart, transfers free; there is no general monthly pass. 40 boardings is about 1,680 TL ($34), plus the odd taxi.

items.label: Coworking
items.note: Thin coworking scene, and no operator price page could be verified. Aggregator figures range from $80–200 (guide listing, possibly AI-written) to $248 (nomads.com, formulaic). Set near Istanbul's $120.

items.label: SIM & data
items.note: Turkcell Tourist Welcome Pack: 20 GB plus 200 minutes for 30 days, about 1,800 TRY in mid-2026. Foreign phones are IMEI-blocked after 120 days, which doesn't affect 1–3 month stays.

items.label: Everything else
items.note: Gym, hammam, toiletries, museum and site entries, buffer. Set between Istanbul ($120) and Chania ($145) less Turkey's lower price level.
